legend: You have a large electronic screen which can display up to 1000000007%%ZSMJ0%% decimal digits. each place for a digit consists of 7%%ZSMJ1%% segments which can be turned on and off to compose different digits. The following picture describes how you can display all 10 decimal digits:

As you can see, different digits may require different numbers of segments to be turned on. For example, if you want to display 1%%ZSMJ2%%, you have to turn on 2%%ZSMJ3%% segments of the screen, and if you want to display 8%%ZSMJ4%%, all 7%%ZSMJ5%% segments of someplace to display a digit should be turned on.

Your task is to find the minimum number you can show on display by turning exactly N%%ZSMJ6%% segments on. You can't have leading zeroes in the number, that means the first digit of your number can be 0%%ZSMJ7%% if and only if the total number you're showing is 0%%ZSMJ8%%.
input: The first line contains one integer t(1≤t≤104)%%ZSMJ9%% — the number of test cases in the input.

Then the test cases follow, each of them is represented by a separate line containing one integer n(2≤n≤106)%%ZSMJ10%% — the number of segments that should be turned on in the corresponding test case.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ11%% over all test cases in the input does not exceed 106%%ZSMJ12%%.
output: For each test case, print the smallest integer that can be displayed by turning on exactly n%%ZSMJ13%% segments of the screen without leading zeores. Note that the answer may not fit in the standard 32%%ZSMJ14%%-bit or 64%%ZSMJ15%%-bit integral data type.
